pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Positive) and Slack channel #p-maymont (Neutral) disagree -- Slack is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Green (100.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (75.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Red (50.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. performance_review_cadence.source: Derived from Gong call titles, trailing 90 days (2026-05-20 to 2026-08-18), matched to account by external-party email domain (not name-fragment keyword matching -- several account names are generic English words/surnames -- Western, Standard, Jones, Brick, Open House, Oakwood -- that would false-positive under substring matching, the same failure class already caught in the Pylon ticket-tone company mismatch). Green requires a recurring, explicitly exec/review-titled meeting found in the window (e.g. 'Weekly Exec Meeting'); Yellow = real call activity in the window but no meeting titled as a business/exec review (most calls are training/implementation/support syncs, which may still reflect a real relationship without a formal QBR cadence); Red = zero matched Gong calls found in the window at all. CAVEAT: Gong call titles in this instance are inconsistently set (some auto-generated as 'Call with X - Y', some manually named) -- this is a best-effort proxy per the rubric's own suggested source ('CSM-entered + Gong (QBR calls tagged)'), not a confirmed absence of QBR practice. A real QBR held under a differently-worded title would be missed.

executive_sponsor_alignment.note: Zero Gong calls matched to this account in the 90-day window -- NOT scored as Red (same domain-matching-gap caveat as performance_review_cadence). Left unscored rather than penalized.
executive_sponsor_alignment.source: Derived from Gong call parties' stated job titles on matched calls, trailing 90 days, same domain-based account matching as performance_review_cadence. pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Only Slack signal available (Gong had zero domain-matched calls in the trailing 90d window). Slack channel #p-hudson: Neutral. Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Green (92.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (100.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Red (50.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

median_ttd_hours.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI, GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01, median(TIME_TO_DECISION_HOURS) split by GROUP_STATUS. Band thresholds empirically reconstructed from the 268-account distribution (no confirmed post-8/18 rubric statement found for this metric) -- provisional, same convention already used for override_rate_pct/support_ticket_ratio_per_100/tes_pct.
median_ttd_hours.declined_qa_hold_diagnostic: 19/375 (5.1%) of declines show a >1h gap between Findigs' own UW decision and the final decision -- a proxy for customer-QA-hold time, NOT the same as the qa_pct row below (different metric, different definition). See project memory for the Beztak investigation this came from.
median_ttd_hours.median_note: Blended median across ALL decisioned groups this quarter (approved+declined+cancelled+passed), for reference only -- NOT what the rubric bands on. The rubric scores 'worse_of_two' (max of the approved-only and declined-only medians) specifically so a slow-decline problem can't hide behind fast, high-volume approvals.

approval_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours.

override_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours. Bands (ENT/MM) Green<=3/Yellow3-6/Red>6, SMB exempted (not gated), per rubric.
override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). The blended 'Has Decision Override' flag also fires when Findigs' internal UW recommendation disagreed with the group's final status even if the group's own visible status never flipped -- something these two directional fields can't see. These are a different, narrower lens (did the group's own recorded outcome flip declined->approved, or approved->declined), not officially banded (no Green/Yellow/Red threshold has been defined for either direction individually) -- shown as raw rate/count only. Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

qa_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours, GROUP_WORKFLOW_STATUS ILIKE '%QA%'. Band thresholds empirically reconstructed per segment (provisional, no confirmed post-8/18 statement found).

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Neutral) and Slack channel #p-elme (Negative) disagree -- Slack is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Positive) and Slack channel #p-western-wealth (Neutral) disagree -- Slack is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (66.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (76.5) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (72.7)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Green (88.9) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (75.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (27.3)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

performance_review_cadence.source: Derived from Gong call titles, trailing 90 days (2026-05-20 to 2026-08-18), matched to account by external-party email domain (not name-fragment keyword matching -- several account names are generic English words/surnames -- Western, Standard, Jones, Brick, Open House, Oakwood -- that would false-positive under substring matching, the same failure class already caught in the Pylon ticket-tone company mismatch). CAVEAT: Gong call titles in this instance are inconsistently set (some auto-generated as 'Call with X - Y', some manually named) -- this is a best-effort proxy per the rubric's own suggested source ('CSM-entered + Gong (QBR calls tagged)'), not a confirmed absence of QBR practice. A real QBR held under a differently-worded title would be missed.

executive_sponsor_alignment.source: Derived from Gong call parties' stated job titles on matched calls, trailing 90 days, same domain-based account matching as performance_review_cadence. Red = no exec-level title seen. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Red does not distinguish 'confirmed no exec engaged' from 'zero Gong call data matched this account in the window' -- see per-account note.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Neutral) and Slack channel #p-kairos (Positive) disagree -- Gong is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

performance_review_cadence.source: Derived from Gong call titles, trailing 90 days (2026-05-20 to 2026-08-18), matched to account by external-party email domain (not name-fragment keyword matching -- several account names are generic English words/surnames -- Western, Standard, Jones, Brick, Open House, Oakwood -- that would false-positive under substring matching, the same failure class already caught in the Pylon ticket-tone company mismatch). pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Only Slack signal available (Gong had zero domain-matched calls in the trailing 90d window). Slack channel #p-open-house-property-management: Positive. Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (74.0) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Red (22.2) | Client Sentiment (20%): Green (100.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Negative) and Slack channel #p-sentral (Neutral) disagree -- Gong is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

median_ttd_hours.declined_qa_hold_diagnostic: 72/76 (94.7%) of declines show a >1h gap between Findigs' own UW decision and the final decision -- a proxy for customer-QA-hold time, NOT the same as the qa_pct row below (different metric, different definition). median_ttd_hours.median_note: Blended median across ALL decisioned groups this quarter (approved+declined+cancelled+passed), for reference only -- NOT what the rubric bands on. The rubric scores 'worse_of_two' (max of the approved-only and declined-only medians) specifically so a slow-decline problem can't hide behind fast, high-volume approvals.

approval_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours.

override_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours. Bands (ENT/MM) Green<=3/Yellow3-6/Red>6, SMB exempted (not gated), per rubric.
override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). The blended 'Has Decision Override' flag also fires when Findigs' internal UW recommendation disagreed with the group's final status even if the group's own visible status never flipped -- something these two directional fields can't see. These are a different, narrower lens (did the group's own recorded outcome flip declined->approved, or approved->declined), not officially banded (no Green/Yellow/Red threshold has been defined for either direction individually) -- shown as raw rate/count only. Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Positive) and Slack channel #p-standard-management (Positive) agree -- classification confirmed by two independent sources. Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (51.1) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (58.8) | Client Sentiment (20%): Green (100.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Gong (Positive) and Slack channel #p-highmark (Neutral) disagree -- Slack is the more negative signal and wins per the 'most-negative-wins' rule (don't let one channel's good news mask the other's bad news). Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (72.2) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (71.1) | Client Sentiment (20%): Yellow (27.3)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). These are a different, narrower lens (did the group's own recorded outcome flip declined->approved, or approved->declined), not officially banded (no Green/Yellow/Red threshold has been defined for either direction individually) -- shown as raw rate/count only. Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). Only Slack signal available (Gong had zero domain-matched calls in the trailing 90d window). Slack channel #p-hrg: Negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.
