client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

median_ttd_hours.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI, GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01, median(TIME_TO_DECISION_HOURS) split by GROUP_STATUS. Band thresholds empirically reconstructed from the 268-account distribution (no confirmed post-8/18 rubric statement found for this metric) -- provisional, same convention already used for override_rate_pct/support_ticket_ratio_per_100/tes_pct.

approval_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours. FS accounts capped at Yellow max per Scoring Matrix V2 ('Cap FS at yellow').

qa_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours, GROUP_WORKFLOW_STATUS ILIKE '%QA%'. Band thresholds empirically reconstructed per segment (provisional, no confirmed post-8/18 statement found).

override_rate_pct.note: Has Decision Override only applies for DecisionAssist accounts (Sigma field definition).
override_rate_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as median_ttd_hours. Bands (ENT/MM) Green<=3/Yellow3-6/Red>6, SMB exempted (not gated), per rubric.

support_ticket_ratio_per_100.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), Support Cases BI, CREATED_AT >= 2026-07-01, CASE_IS_DELETED=false, excludes CASE_USER_TYPE ILIKE '%applic%' or '%guarant%' or NULL. Recalibrated thresholds (Green<=15, Yellow15-50, Red>50) per 2026-08-18 fix.

tes_pct.note: 0 PM support cases this quarter -- 0% is a real zero, not a data gap.
tes_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- same population as support_ticket_ratio_per_100; numerator = Support Case Has Tech Escalation. Segment-aware thresholds (ENT Green<=3/Yellow3-6/Red>6, MM Green<2/Yellow2-5/Red>5, SMB provisional) per 2026-08-18 note.

volume_trend_pct.source: Refreshed 2026-09-02 -- Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI, trailing 90d vs prior 90d, GROUP_IS_SUBMITTED=true. revenue_trend_quarterly.source: Sigma Core (Data Model) Revenue Actual BI -- SUM(FINDIGS_REVENUE_AMOUNT) grouped by rollup company and calendar quarter. Q3 2026 is partial, through 2026-09-02. QoQ% compares the two most recent COMPLETE quarters (Q1 vs Q2) to avoid a misleading full-vs-partial comparison. Supersedes revenue_trend_mom_pct for display; that field is retained for reference only.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (50.8) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (66.7) | Client Sentiment (20%): Red (50.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (64.9) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (50.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Green (100.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Yellow (65.1) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Green (100.0) | Client Sentiment (20%): Green (100.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

composite_score_partial.why: Platform & Product Metrics (50%): Red (48.4) | Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship (30%): Yellow (66.7) | Client Sentiment (20%): Green (100.0)
composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.completed_applications_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 1). Sigma Core (Data Model), User Application Funnel (PostHog-sourced), FIRST_EVENT_AT >= 2026-07-01. completed_applications_90d = SUM(HIT_SUBMIT); application_funnel_total_90d = COUNT(*) (all funnel participants in window); rate = submit/total. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.
accounts.groups_submitted_vs_expected_source: Added 2026-09-02 -- unscored, contextual, PROVISIONAL benchmark (2026-09-02 meeting, Phase 2). No 'expected'/'target' groups-submitted field exists anywhere in Sigma -- confirmed via two separate thorough searches this session (Core Data Model incl. Groups BI/CSM Company Analysis/UW Group States BI, Benchmark Report, Findigs Customers, Rollup Companies, Weekly Performance Metrics DecisionAssist/Fullscreen, QBR). groups_submitted_expected_90d is DERIVED, not a real Sales/CS target: portfolio-median rate of (groups submitted trailing 90d / live units) = 0.1540, computed across 257 accounts with both values populated, applied to this account's own unit_count_live_current_month. Checked per-segment (ENT/MM/SMB) and the medians were within 0.007 of each other -- not different enough to justify segment-specific rates, so one portfolio-wide rate is used. Treat as a rough baseline only; replace with a real Sales/CS-set target if/when one exists. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. Occupies the exact same weighted-composite slot gong_call_sentiment held before (same weight: 6/6/4 pts ENT/MM/SMB per 'CS Client Health Scoring' Scoring Matrix) -- pylon_ticket_tone is untouched, still its own separate row/weight.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

client_communication_sentiment.source: Added 2026-09-02 -- REPLACES gong_call_sentiment per Emma's direction (2026-09-02): 'client communication sentiment' now combines Gong call sentiment (same methodology as before: direct Gong REST API, domain-matched, trailing 90d, 3-tier Positive/Neutral/Negative) with a new Slack signal (per-account #p-<company> channel, read + hand-classified by the same 3-tier rubric, trailing ~90d or last ~100 messages). Combination rule: when both sources exist, the MORE NEGATIVE of the two wins (not an average) -- this is deliberate: the motivating case is Elme Communities, where Pylon ticket tone read Positive/Green right up to a churn driven by external REIT liquidation, because a disengaging account files fewer tickets, not more. Averaging would have let a good signal dilute a bad one; this rubric refuses to do that on either input. When only one source exists, that source is used directly -- missing coverage on one side is not treated as evidence of negative (same principle Gong's own scoring already used). No Gong calls domain-matched in the trailing 90d window AND no Slack channel found/read for this account -- unscored, a coverage gap not evidence of negative. NOT folded into composite_score_partial or pillar_scores.client_sentiment for this account: the whole Client Sentiment pillar (both gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone before it) is DA-only by existing design -- FS composite is deliberately churn-risk-anchored only (csm_qualitative_risk_flag), per Emma's 2026-08-18/19 design, and that boundary applies to this Slack-derived signal too, not just Gong. Populated here as unscored/contextual reference only, same precedent as other FS-excluded fields (e.g. PMS Integration Depth) that are still refreshed for visibility without touching the score.

accounts.sold_vs_live_units_source: Contextual, unscored (added 2026-09-02; meaning corrected 2026-09-04 per Emma). total_units_sold_hubspot = SUM(units__c) across the account's HubSpot closed-won deals, matched via findigs_company_id (pipe-list membership, per project convention). NOTE: units__c represents the account's TOTAL unit count (entire portfolio, all units), NOT incremental units sold in that deal. sold_vs_live_units_pct = live units on Findigs / total units * 100 = share of the client's portfolio live on Findigs. Values well under 100% flag unrealized footprint; values over 100% usually mean the HubSpot total is stale (portfolio grew since the deal) or the Sigma rollup spans more entities than the deal covered. Field names kept for display compatibility; read 'sold' as 'total'. Not folded into pillar_scores or composite_score_partial.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.

composite_score_partial.methodology: REBUILT 2026-09-03 per the 2026-09-02 Alex/Emma meeting decision: the overall composite is now a two-level rollup instead of one flat 19-row weighted average. Each of the 3 pillars already computes its own value/band from its own rows (unchanged -- see pillar_scores). The overall band is now a weighted roll-up of the 3 pillars' VALUES at Platform & Product Metrics 50% / Strategic Alignment, Governance & Relationship 30% / Client Sentiment 20% (Emma's corrected weights from the meeting -- 'let's try that and we can both think about this a little more,' not yet formally final), re-normalized to whichever pillars have real (non-null) data. Overall BAND floor rule, mirroring the same floor-gate philosophy already used at the row level and pillar level everywhere else in this rubric (and the Gong+Slack most-negative-wins combination): any single Red pillar forces the overall band to at least Yellow; 2 or more Red pillars forces Red; a Green overall requires ALL included pillars to be Green -- a Green-heavy weighted average alone is not enough, deliberately, so one weak pillar can't get diluted into invisibility by two good ones. The CSM Churn Risk Flag (qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance.csm_qualitative_risk_flag) is kept as an explicit hard override forcing the overall band to Red regardless of the pillar math, per Alex's explicit instruction on the call to keep it 'forcing Red on its own.' The displayed VALUE is always the true weighted average of the 3 pillar values, never flattened to match a forced band, per the existing 2026-08-19 design principle (value = severity/triage signal, band = categorical gate). This replaces the prior flat-19-row-weighted-average-with-global-floor-gate composite; that computation is preserved below under old_flat_composite_for_reference for anyone comparing before/after.
